items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: Mike’s style as a pianist is based on those of Oscar Peterson and Bud Powell

ctx.x: I’ll say it this way. There are no wrong notes but there are wrong lines. And so relief is a half step away. And so Dizzy and Miles and those cats, they were masters of non- harmonic tones with the proper resolutions. Because the whole chromatic scale can be related to one triad if you resolve everything properly. And so if you land wrong, man, you could make it an appoggiatura, a step up into the chord. And so Dizzy, he was a master at it. So was Charlie Parker. So there are only wrong notes if you play the…

Well said. I wanted to read something about you from the three volume Grove Dictionary of Jazz, which you’re in. And this person, whoever wrote this, he says, “Mike’s style as a pianist is based on those of Oscar Peterson and Bud Powell, to which he has added a personal and contemplative approach.”

Well I play like me. You see I never did any of that transcribing. First of all transcribing to me is the greatest ear training in the world but you can not learn to play from transcribing, which is a big mistake they’re making in the jazz ed departments. Because that’s not you. You’re playing somebody else’s — they say well that’s vocabulary. That’s not the way people learn vocabulary. When you’re a child you learn a vocabulary. Apple. Give me the apple. You take the apple. You don’t learn — you don’t repeat a…
